title: Exact tensor by an integral line commutes with the augmented strict Roos complex
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $X$ be any scheme, and let $R$ be its completed coefficient sheaf [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $T$ be an $R$-module sheaf locally free of rank one. Put $T_0=T[0]$ and $F(P)=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R T_0)$, using the actual signed total-tensor model [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then $T_0$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $F$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism. For every good complex $P$ (K-flat with flat terms, as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]), $F(P)$ is good and there is an isomorphism $\rho_P:F(\operatorname{Roos}(K_\bullet(P)))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Roos}(K_\bullet(F(P)))$ with $F(u_P)\,;\,\rho_P=u_{F(P)}$. Here $K_\bullet$ is the actual termwise quotient tower, $\operatorname{Roos}=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, and $u_P=(c_P,0)$ is its specified augmentation [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. No derived-completeness assumption is made.

proof.text: On a cover trivializing T, tensor by T is the identity. Exact slice restriction detects exactness, and sectionwise products identify the canonical product comparison with the identity locally. Hence tensor by T is exact and preserves countable products. Total tensor with T[0] is its termwise complex functor, so it preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. The K-flat total-tensor theorem and flatness of terms show that good complexes stay good.

proof.text: The balanced finite comparison sends a tensor (x tensor y) to (a tensor x) tensor y; its inverse recombines these tensors. These sheafified maps commute with quotient transitions and augmentations. Tensor preserves the countable products and the finite biproducts in the mapping cocone, so these comparisons give rho commuting with 1 minus shift and the signed differential. Its product coordinate on the tensored unit is the canonical augmentation, and its second coordinate is zero. The two cone projections prove the unit equation.

lean.statement:
theorem integralLine_roosTensor
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t})
    (T : Mod l E X none) [T.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1] :
    let T₀ := (HomologicalComplex.single (Mod l E X none) (.up ℤ) 0).obj T
    let F := (Functor.prod' (𝟭 (Cx l E X none))
      ((Functor.const (Cx l E X none)).obj T₀)) ⋙
        coefficientTotalTensor.{u, t + 1, t} (topology X none) (ring l E X none)
    CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients
        (J := topology X none) (R := ring l E X none) T₀ ∧
      (∀ (A B : Cx l E X none) (f : A ⟶ B), QuasiIso f → QuasiIso (F.map f)) ∧
      ∀ P : (Good l E X none).FullSubcategory,
        Good l E X none (F.obj P.obj) ∧
          ∃ ρ : F.obj (integralOperationsRoos ((tower l E X none).obj P.obj)) ≅
              integralOperationsRoos ((tower l E X none).obj (F.obj P.obj)),
            F.map (roosUnit l E X none P.obj) ≫ ρ.hom =
              roosUnit l E X none (F.obj P.obj)
